definition: WildJailbreak is an adversarial jailbreak-prompt benchmark used in SafeChain (systematically evaluating 13 large reasoning models' safety on StrongReject/WildJailbreak, finding no model is safe on both) and PAM (training large reasoning models to explicitly assess which human-preference priority, e.g. harmlessness, applies to a query before reasoning).

evidence.note: SafeChain systematically evaluates 13 large reasoning models' safety on StrongReject/WildJailbreak, finding no model is safe on both, that unsafe responses are consistently longer than safe ones, that safety improves within a model family as it scales but long-CoT fine-tuning itself does not inherently improve safety over the base instruction-tuned model, and that training-free decoding strategies controlling thought length (ZeroThink most effectively) improve safety without training -- motivating a new CoT-style safety training dataset that preserves reasoning performance while improving safety.
evidence.title: SafeChain: Safety of Language Models with Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Capabilities

evidence.note: PAM trains large reasoning models to explicitly assess which human-preference priority (e.g. harmlessness) applies to a query before reasoning -- via a Flavell-metacognition-inspired cold-start SFT stage plus DPO preference optimization -- improving helpfulness, harmlessness and instruction-following by an average of ~10 points over an identically-trained model without this metacognitive step, without a corresponding drop in math reasoning performance for one of two backbones.
evidence.title: PAM: Enhancing General Alignment of Large Reasoning Models through Priority-Aware Metacognition

name: WildJailbreak
